canonical_topic: Conversion efficiency of a solar unit
definition: Conversion efficiency is the fraction of absorbed solar energy that a collector turns into usable output energy — most solar collectors can only absorb certain wavelengths, and much incoming light is reflected or otherwise lost before it can be converted.
core_idea: A solar installation's total output depends on two separate factors multiplying together: how much solar energy is available/absorbed at the site, and how efficiently the unit converts that absorbed energy into useful energy.
key_points: Conversion efficiency is described as a ratio of energy produced to energy absorbed.
Solar collectors are limited to certain usable wavelengths; light outside that range is reflected or absorbed without being converted.
Both site solar-energy availability and unit conversion efficiency jointly determine an installation's output — they are separate levers, not one combined figure.
relationships: Combines with site solar-resource quality (geographic/atmospheric factors) to determine total installation output.
trading_implications: Rated conversion efficiency is a key spec for comparing solar equipment/technologies when underwriting an installation's expected output.
caveats: Confusing conversion efficiency (produced vs. absorbed) with an all-in efficiency that already accounts for how much ambient sunlight was captured/absorbed in the first place.

formulas.name: Conversion efficiency (conceptual)
formulas.formula: conversion efficiency = energy produced / energy absorbed

variables.energy produced: useful energy output of the solar unit
variables.energy absorbed: solar energy absorbed by the collector before conversion losses
